verses.1: In the year of Darius, son of Ahasuerus, from the line of Medes, who ruled over the kingdom of Kashdim.
verses.2: In one of his reigns, I, Daniel, wrote down the years in the books of records. These were the years when Jehovah spoke to the prophet Jeremiah about the destruction of Jerusalem over seventy years.
verses.3: And I turned my face toward the God of heaven, in order to pray. I also offered sacrifices, incense, and other offerings.
verses.4: And I glorified the LORD my God, and I said, “You are the great and glorious God who keeps the covenant and the mercy for those who love You and obey Your commands.”
verses.5: We have sinned and been rebellious. We have broken your laws and judgments.
verses.6: And we did not hear from our servants, the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, princes, and ancestors, and to all the people of the earth.
verses.7: To you, O God of righteousness, may we have peace today, for the sake of all Jews and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, as well as for all Israel, both those who are close by and those who are far away, in all the lands where they were banished in eternity.
verses.8: May the LORD give us strength for our kings, our rulers, and our ancestors who sinned against You.
verses.9: To our merciful Lord and Savior, please have mercy on us, for we have sinned against You.
verses.10: And we did not hear the voice of our God, saying that we should follow His commandments, which He gave us through His servants, the prophets.
verses.11: And all of Israel failed to obey your commandments. They refused to listen to your voice. Thus, those curses were inflicted upon us. These curses are written in Moses’ laws, which are the laws of God’s people. We have sinned against them.
verses.12: And he made known his words, which were about us and about our judgments. Those judgments were meant to bring us great harm, but such harm never happened under heaven, as it did in Jerusalem.
verses.13: As it is written in Moses’ Torah, all this evil has come upon us. It has not pleased the Lord our God to let us be saved from it. May He truly forgive us and heal us in His true love.
verses.14: And Jehovah will deal with the evil ones, and He will bring it upon us. For Jehovah our God is righteous; He does what He says, and we do not listen to His words.
verses.15: And now, O Lord our God, who have brought your people out of Egypt with strength and power, we have sinned and become wicked today.
verses.16: O Adonai, as you are righteous, please let your wrath and punishment be upon Jerusalem, your holy city. For in our sins and transgressions, along with the sins of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people will be brought to shame in all around us.
verses.17: And now, hear our Lord’s prayers and supplications. May His glory be revealed upon Your holy place, for the sake of Adonai.
verses.18: O Lord, hear your ear! Open your eyes and see what we have done. The city that is called after your name… It’s not because of our righteous deeds that we are being punished before you. It’s because of your great mercy.
verses.19: O Lord, hear me! O Lord, have mercy on me! Listen to me and do not delay in answering my prayers. For your name is called upon for your city and your people.
verses.20: And I still speak, and I pray, and I confess my sins and the sins of my people, Israel. I also ask for forgiveness from Jehovah, my God, on the Holy Mountain.
verses.21: And yet, I am still talking about prayer. And the man who I saw in my vision at the beginning… he reached out to me with a kind gesture, as if to offer me some kind of gift.
verses.22: And he built a house for me, and he spoke with me. He said, “Daniel, now I have gone to teach you in the wilderness.”
verses.23: At the beginning of your stay here, something came forth. I come to say that you are worthy of honor. And in this matter, there is also a child who is born.
verses.24: Seventy-seven times will it be poured upon your people and upon your holy city, for all their sins and transgressions. It will bring about judgment and destruction of evil. It will also bring justice to the world, and it will destroy all idols and prophets. It will sanctify what is sacred.
verses.25: And you shall know and understand from what has been revealed, so that Jerusalem can be rebuilt until the time of the Messiah comes. Seventy-two years will pass, and then it will be rebuilt, both the inner and outer parts of the city.
verses.26: And after seventy years, the Messiah will be recognized. But he will not have the city and the Holy Place. The wicked will destroy them. They will be scattered throughout the land, and war will continue until the end.
verses.27: And the covenant shall be increased for many. One half of the people shall be gathered together, and they shall offer sacrifices and offerings. And on their shoulders shall be placed the symbols of their offerings. And all these things shall be carried away along with them.
